Seminar Title:

Climate Change and the Paradigms of Food Security— Risk, Resilience, and Policy Pathways for Asia and Africa

Seminar Type:

Contact:

Abstract:

Attaining food security and environmental sustainability, particularly through emissions reduction to mitigate climate change, is fundamental to economic development. While ensuring food security is essential for poverty reduction and ending hunger, climate action is equally crucial for limiting climate-induced economic losses and achieving long-term sustainable development. The United Nations&rsquo Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2030 Agenda underscores this dual imperativeness through SDG 2 (Zero hunger) and SDG 13 (Climate Action). However, existing literature lacks cross-country studies that simultaneously address these interconnected issues, particularly for Asia and Africa. Against this backdrop, this study focuses on Asian and African countries from 2000 to 2023. Ensuring food security in Asia and Africa is critical amid changing market dynamics, food-energy price inflation, and geopolitical risks, alongside climate shocks. Thus, this study contributes to the existing literature through these four objectives. First, it assesses coordinated development between food security and climate resilience using the coupling and coordination degree (CCD) analysis. Understanding CCD pathways reveals food security vulnerabilities to climate change and identifies whether development exhibits trade-offs or synergies between food security and climate resilience across Asian and African countries. Second, this study examines the roles of agricultural green total factor productivity (GTFP) and agricultural investments in determining food security, while accounting for the effects of climate change. Third, food security not only depends on agriculture but also on the choice of other goods and services. Particularly, energy security plays a crucial role in agrifood systems however, many Asian and African countries face the dual challenge of ensuring food and energy security due to various factors. Thus, the third objective assesses how pricing mechanism (food-to-energy price ratio) and financial and trade sanctions affect food and energy security, while examining climate change&rsquos threshold effects.&nbsp Fourth, this study investigates whether climate solutions (adaptive capacity and climate finance) enhance food security and address climate change, while underscoring the moderating role of government effectiveness. The findings underscore the need for tailored policy interventions to support sustainable agriculture, increase domestic climate finance and strengthen multisectoral adaptive capacity through proactive climate policies and decentralized governance systems to accelerate SDG progress across Asia and Africa.
